finding.summary: Materializing `lineAffinity: 'backward'` on every caret position leaks into keyboard-built selection *anchors*, silently overriding the documented asymmetric start default
finding.evidence: The approach in docs/tasks/active/20260822-caret-line-affinity-todo.md:29 says a caret position "always states its reading (materialized, defaulting to 'backward')" while "absent stays reserved for endpoints from other producers … which keep computeSelectionRects' asymmetric default". But selection anchors are built *from the caret*: text-editor.ts:2774 (`const anchor = this.selection.range?.anchor ?? pos`), :2807 and :2826 (`?? this.cursor.position`). Previously `cursor.position` carried no affinity, so `buildRects` applied `start.lineAffinity ?? 'forward'` (packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:260) — the default that exists specifically so a highlight does not open on a zero-width sliver of the line above (docs/design/docs/docs-local-caret-anchoring.md:82-88). After this change those anchors arrive with an explicit `'backward'`, so a shift-selection whose normalized *start* is the caret at a wrap boundary now resolves the start with the backward reading instead of the forward one. Neither the new design-doc paragraph nor any test records this behavioural consequence of the 'always materialize' decision.

verdict.reason: The mechanics are real (cursor.ts:26/52-56 always materializes affinity; text-editor.ts:2774/2807/2826 build anchors from the caret; selection.ts:260 defaults an affinity-less start to 'forward'), but the finding is not blocking under the design-fit rubric. (a) Design-doc discipline is satisfied and the claim that the doc doesn't record it is inaccurate: docs/design/docs/docs-local-caret-anchoring.md:89-101 folds the decision into the canonical subsystem doc (linked at docs/design/README.md:55), stating the caret "always materializes its reading ('backward' unless told otherwise)", that the value "travels with the position into presence, undo history, selection endpoints and rendering", and that absent is reserved for other producers which keep the asymmetric default. (b) No acceptance criterion of the originating task is unmet — docs/tasks/active/20260822-caret-line-affinity-todo.md:55-61 lists peer caret/highlight alignment, edits not erasing affinity, Home/arrow carets publishing affinity, and a call-site regression test, all covered by packages/docs/test/view/caret-line-affinity.test.ts. (c) No Non-Goal is exceeded: docs/tasks/active/20260822-selection-line-affinity-todo.md:60-67 keeps the standalone caret's 'backward' reading unchanged (preserved here), and its acceptance criterion at :18-26 records that a backward-affinity start on a boundary yields only a zero-width, invisible first rect. What remains — the precise rendering consequence and the absence of a test pinning it — belongs to the correctness and test-adequacy lenses, and as a design-doc wording-granularity remark it is at most minor, which never blocks.
